target_customer: Large organizations in healthcare, retail and logistics with legacy software and big back-office workloads
problem: Enterprises want AI agents but their critical work runs through legacy systems without APIs; Refactor builds agents that call, click and navigate them, with a focus on reliability and security.
business_model: enterprise services and software for custom AI agent deployments
product_category: enterprise AI agents for legacy software (related launch Blast for AI red-teaming)

founders.name: Daniel Zamoshchin
education: Stanford, computer science with security focus
previous_startups: High school app with over 2M downloads (name not given)
founders.background_notes: Security research with Prof. Dan Boneh and data privacy research with Prof. Matei Zaharia, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that operate legacy UIs and phone calls need reliability engineering around then-new computer-use models, but rely on third-party models.

defensibility.rationale: Custom deployments embed with customers, but the approach is replicable by RPA vendors and model providers shipping computer use.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A search found Anthropic introduced computer use in 2024 and AWS later offered WorkSpaces for agents; no source ties these to Refactor specifically.

market_need_then: YC page says it worked with companies with 50B+ in annual revenue; a job post cites healthcare reimbursement labor cost of 50B+; no independent spend evidence.

branding.community_and_virality: No community or press on the brand found; searches returned only Refactor Games, an unrelated studio.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic developer term shared with many products and an unrelated game studio; the brand search surfaced no coverage of this company.

outcome_analysis: Refactor is a three person YC Summer 2024 team of Stanford friends that sells custom AI agents to large enterprises and also launched Blast for red-teaming enterprise AI. No funding beyond YC, public customers, exit or shutdown was found, and the company website blocked fetching, so the outcome is unknown rather than failed.
notes: The company site refactor.co returned HTTP 402 to a fetch, so it was not read (not worked around). Funding search found no amounts. Searches for the company name returned Refactor Games (layoffs July 2026), which is unrelated. Competitor search returned only generic 2025 to 2026 computer-use articles, so list is empty. Job post mentions a healthcare billing focus and Palo Alto location; the Stanford Daily article found was about a different company (Paratus Health).
